ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the right triangle has its right-angled vertex at the coordinate origin, $\angle OAB=30^\circ$. If point A lies on the graph of the inverse proportional function $y=\frac{6}{x}$ $(x>0)$, what is the value of $k$ in the inverse proportional function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ passing through point B?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $BC\perp x$ axis at point $C$ through point $B$, and draw $AD\perp x$ axis at point $D$ through point $A$, as shown in the figure.\\
$\because \angle BOA=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOC+\angle AOD=90^\circ$,\\
$\because \angle AOD+\angle OAD=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOC=\angle OAD$,\\
Also, $\because \angle BCO=\angle ADO=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \triangle BCO\sim \triangle ODA$,\\
$\therefore \frac{OB}{OA}=\tan30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
$\therefore \frac{{S}_{\triangle BCO}}{{S}_{\triangle ODA}}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
$\because \frac{1}{2}\times AD\times DO=\frac{1}{2}xy=3$,\\
$\therefore {S}_{\triangle BCO}=\frac{1}{2}\times BC\times CO=\frac{1}{3}{S}_{\triangle ODA}=1$,\\
$\because$ The graph of the inverse proportion function that passes through point $B$ is in the second quadrant,\\
therefore, the equation of the inverse proportion function is: $y=-\frac{2}{x}$,\\
$\therefore k=\boxed{-2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, and O is the coordinate origin. Line segment OA points from O to point A in the first quadrant, and A is located on one branch of an inverse proportional function curve in the first quadrant; line segment OB points from O to point B in the second quadrant, and B is located near another branch curve in the second quadrant. Line segment AB connects A and B, triangle OAB is marked with a right angle at O, and the problem gives ∠OAB=30°. In the figure, B is to the left of the y-axis and above the x-axis, so B is in the second quadrant. Reasoning: According to the method, draw AD perpendicular to the x-axis, with foot D; draw BC perpendicular to the x-axis, with foot C. Because OA ⟂ OB, ∠BOA=90°, and from the angle relationships formed by the coordinate axes and perpendicular lines, ∠BOC+∠AOD=90° can be obtained. Also because in right triangle OAD, ∠AOD+∠OAD=90°, so ∠BOC=∠OAD. And ∠BCO=∠ADO=90°, therefore △BCO ∼ △ODA. In right triangle OAB, ∠OAB=30°, so OB/OA=tan30°=1/√3. Therefore the area ratio of the similar triangles is S_{△BCO}/S_{△ODA}=(OB/OA)^2=1/3. Let A=(x_A,y_A). A is on y=6/x, and x>0, so x_A y_A=6. Thus the area of △ODA is (1/2)·OD·AD=(1/2)x_A y_A=3. Therefore S_{△BCO}=3×(1/3)=1. Let B=(x_B,y_B). The area of △BCO is (1/2)|x_B y_B|=1, so |x_B y_B|=2. From the image it can be seen that B is in the second quadrant, x_B<0, y_B>0, therefore x_B y_B<0. The inverse proportional function y=k/x passing through B satisfies k=x_B y_B, so k=-2.
